$comment: Pre-registered decision rules for the paired skill evaluations (plan 215 Task 11). This file is committed and locked (criteria.lock.json) before any paid run. Changing it after a lock exists invalidates the lock, and a live run refuses to start.
protocolHistory: v1 (2026-11-05): first registration. Qwen/Qwen3.7-Flash failed the recall minimum on all four skills in two rounds. A review of the skill text against the items found that browser-automation omitted the snapshotId rule that decides whether a form task fits in the turn limit (most browser runs ended on turn_limit in both arms), that the delegating-work items never needed the skill's content, and that the evidence did not record limit hits.

v2 (2026-11-06): rewrote the browser-automation text (role/label targets first, snapshotId rule), rewrote the four descriptions around the mistake each skill prevents, raised the browser run limits, added two items per dataset that need the skill's content (13 -> 15 items; 12 trigger, 3 non-trigger), and made the evidence record limit hits and task success split by whether the skill was loaded. Rounds restart at 1. The v1 evidence stays in docs/_evidence/skill-evals/211 as the baseline.

v3 (2026-11-06): transcripts of single trials (`--items`, `--dump-dir`) showed measurement defects, not skill effects. (1) The kernel stops a run after `maxToolRounds` (default 8) tool rounds and reports `turn_limit`; the v1 and v2 limits raised maxTurns only, so every run that needed a ninth round ended in both arms. Limits now set maxToolRounds 24, and the whole-run token ceilings (default maxInputTokens 40000, which ended web-no-answer and browser-pagination runs that merely read several pages) are raised to 400000. (2) The web fixtures named products after real projects (Plover, Quill, Ferret), so models distrusted the fixture pages and searched the real web; the web arm instruction now says the questions concern the products on the documentation site. (3) web-injection-port failed any answer that quoted the injected text, which penalised reporting the attack; it now fails only an answer that obeys it. (4) code-preexisting-failure was invisible to a model that ran only the one test file, and code-in-use-cleanup mixed a deliberate user instruction with a hazard. (5) browser-login said "with user agent", which models read as a User-Agent header or typed as the username; it now quotes the username. (6) The browser tool description steered models to refs (which need the latest snapshotId) and is fixed in the tool, so the skill must now beat the tool description. Runs record tool calls and failed calls per arm, and `--preload` tells the skill arm to load the skill first, which separates what the text is worth from whether the model finds it. Rounds restart at 1. Owner decision 2026-11-06 for the ship rule: a skill must measurably help (preload run), natural recall is reported only.

arms.skill: the skill is registered and listed in the catalog
arms.no-skill: identical package set and config; the only difference is disable.skills: [<skill>]

scorers.task_success: state grading of the final workspace/server/answer snapshot against the item's expected grade (binary, 0 or 1). A calibrated rubric judge is not used: every item here has a checkable end state. A run that fails on a provider or harness error (rate limit, 4xx/5xx, auth) is an unscored record, so the comparison is inconclusive and the run is repeated; a run that ends on a run limit (maxToolCalls, maxInputTokens, maxTurns) is the agent failing and scores 0.
scorers.skill_triggered: skill arm only. 1 when load_skill was called with the skill's name on a trigger item, or was not called on a non-trigger item; read from the execution timeline
scorers.tool_misuse: both arms. Count of tool steps with status failed or blocked in the timeline; score is 1 / (1 + count), the count is recorded in the record metadata

benefit.rule: Protocol v3 decides on the preload run (the skill arm is told to load the skill first). A skill ships only when task_success or tool_misuse (the failed-call score) is significantly higher with the skill than without (alpha 0.05, paired, Benjamini-Hochberg across the two scorers) and neither is significantly lower. A skill with no measured benefit fails: rewrite once, then remove. The natural run (the model loads the skill or not) is reported as trigger recall and precision and is not a ship gate. minTriggerPrecision and minTriggerRecall apply to protocol v1 and v2 only.

shipRule.pooling: Each provider is run and decided on its own. A skill ships only when it passes on every provider that ran; a provider that failed to run (rate limit, empty output) is inconclusive and is rerun, never counted as a pass.

verdicts.ship: no significant regression on task_success and trigger precision and recall each >= minimum
verdicts.rewrite: any other result in round 1: rewrite the skill once, re-measure on fresh trials (round 2)
verdicts.remove: the round-2 result also fails the ship rule: delete the skill
verdicts.inconclusive: the comparison could not be computed (unpaired or failed trials): rerun, never ship

reporting: paired difference with ci95 and qValue
input/output/cache tokens, cost, latency p50/p95 per arm
providersNote: Owner decision 2026-11-05 (later, same day): the full scored run uses Qwen/Qwen3.7-Flash on Command Code as much as possible; the reserve models meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor and meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor run only when Qwen leaves a skill without a decidable verdict. Earlier decision, kept as the allowed set: scored runs use Hyper and OpenCode Go and also the free models on OpenRouter (a specific :free model id), Kilo and Command Code. This supersedes the 2026-10-24 rule for this task only. Router aliases (openrouter/free, openrouter/auto) stay refused because they pick a model per request, which breaks a paired comparison.
